clips.title: The story
paras: Camping 101: Skinning guides skilled hide-gatherers to Bloodhoof Village to expand their practical field craft. Under the instruction of Yonn Deepcut, skinners learn to fashion beast pelts into comfortable Camp Chairs for wilderness survival. This training emphasizes the importance of rest and preparation when journeying far beyond the safety of civilization.

Harvesting the hides and pelts of fallen beasts is one of the most practical survival skills on Azeroth. Beyond tanning leather for armor and gear, a resourceful skinner can turn rough animal skins into wilderness comforts. For travelers who spend long weeks traversing wild territories, learning how to work hides into resting equipment makes the difference between exhaustion and staying sharp in combat.

In Mulgore, skinners are directed to Bloodhoof Village to speak with Yonn Deepcut. Once a skinner demonstrates basic proficiency in harvesting beast hides, Yonn imparts the craft of stitching together a Camp Chair. Settlers in towns and villages do not welcome travelers pitching tents in the middle of streets, so these chairs are designed specifically for wilderness use, paired with a crackling campfire taught by local cooks.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Being able to skillfully harvest the skins and hides of fallen beasts is one of the more valuable skills an adventurer can possess.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft a Camp Chair for your camp. Sometimes it's important to just take a load off, and you can use some of those hides you've gathered to make a comfy chair to sit in. A bit of relaxation can help ensure that you are at your peak condition and can strike where it counts the next time you find yourself in a dust-up.

clips.title: Completion
paras: There you have it, you can now craft your very own Camp Chair. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.
